scene_translation: When you turned the key, the old door slowly opened. Inside was a small altar, and in the faint light, a notebook had been placed there. Opening it, you found written in blue ink: 'Testo-san, next go to the old clock tower at Suidobashi. By ten o'clock at night.' There was a sound from behind you — turning around, an elderly man who appeared to be the shrine's priest was standing there. 'To think you know about this room… Were you asked by the woman in the blue kimono?'
grammar_note: 【〜とは】This expression marks something as surprising or unexpected — the priest says 「この<ruby>部屋<rt>へや</rt></ruby>のことを<ruby>知<rt>し</rt></ruby>っているとは」, meaning 'to think that you know about this room…' It carries a tone of quiet astonishment and is often left unfinished, letting the feeling hang in the air. Note also the priest's speech style: 〜かね is a gentle, old-fashioned masculine ending, warmer and more reflective than plain だ — a register quite different from the casual じゃん of younger characters.

mystery_memo: The notebook has now revealed the next destination: the clock tower at Suidobashi, by 10 PM. The woman in blue knows the player's name and has been orchestrating each step — locker, shrine, now this. The elderly shrine priest (宮司) recognizes the blue-kimono woman and seems unsurprised by her involvement, suggesting a prior relationship with the shrine; his tone is cautious but not hostile. Relationship status: priest is neutral-watchful. The notebook and key are now confirmed as a matched set left deliberately for the player.
